solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S025-01.notes: Borrowed rhythms, images and phrases = derivative. 'Innovative' is the opposite; 'obscure' and 'prolific' are not supported. One routine vocabulary step, though 'derivative' may be unfamiliar to some students.

flags: minor: the passage's own word 'errors' practically gives away 'erroneous', so the item barely tests vocabulary; a less obvious key such as 'inaccurate' or 'unreliable', or removing 'errors', would test more
S025-02.notes: Islands misplaced or left off = erroneous. 'Meticulous' and 'comprehensive' contradict the passage; 'ornamental' is irrelevant.

S025-03.notes: Text 2 places the sister abroad for all of 1792 and has a neighbor sitting for the painter in winter 1792, which directly undercuts the claim in Text 1. B contradicts Text 2; nothing in either text supports C or D.

S025-04.notes: Moving the landmarks did not lower the recovery rate, so the stones and logs were not the main cue. B overstates the finding (the rates were about equal); A and D are unsupported.

S025-05.notes: Logical comparison: a hyena's bite force should be compared with a lion's bite force, so the singular 'that of a' is needed. A compares a bite force with a lion; B's 'those' disagrees in number with 'bite force'; C is ungrammatical. This is the standard concept with a familiar trap.

S025-06.notes: The two groups ran tests at the same time, so 'Meanwhile' fits. There is no cause, example or contrast to support the other transitions.

S025-07.notes: Only B states the length of the restoration (twelve years, 2009 to 2021). D gives only the end date.

S025-08.notes: A comma follows an introductory dependent clause before the main clause. A semicolon or colon needs an independent clause before it; leaving out punctuation is the usual tempting error.

flags: minor: choice D does the subtraction for the student (1,600 vs. 600 and 800), so the item needs no data work; stating the raw summer and winter values would make students compute the drops
S025-09.notes: Checked the drops: 600, 800 and 1,600. Only D compares the drops across groups. B gives a single value and C is true but does not show which drop was largest.

flags: minor: 'unsure whether they had played very badly or very well' is almost a restatement of choice B, so the inference is close to literal
S025-10.notes: The musicians were unsure how the conductor judged them. A contradicts 'unsure', C is unsupported, and D reverses the order of events.
